item.title: Improving AI Agent Performance Through Context and Priority-Based Prompting
item.description:
Improving AI Agent Performance Through Context and Priority-Based Prompting

Recent advancements in frontier AI models have shifted how agents fail; rather than being confused by instructions, modern agents typically make incorrect assumptions about a user’s goals or priorities.

🔍 Overview

Early AI agents required precise instructions to avoid performing the wrong tasks. Current models are more capable but may still produce suboptimal results if they lack context on priorities. For example, GPT-6-Astra may produce minified code if it assumes it is writing for itself, though it is capable of producing acceptable Golang code when told that humans will be reading it.

⚙️ Key details

To optimize agent performance, users are encouraged to provide broad context and relative priorities rather than just a concrete technical spec. This approach allows models to offer meaningful input on broader goals.

  • Contextual Prompting: Sharing the overall project aim and personal priorities (e.g., keeping a laptop cool) can lead to improvements that an explicit spec might miss, such as choosing a Gradient model over EditLens or using native messaging for a local model.
  • Relative Priorities: In professional settings, specifying the relative importance of factors—such as avoiding bugs, observability, performance, and fitting into current code—allows the model to understand which elements can be traded off to achieve others.
  • Codebase Adaptation: Agents are smart enough to pick up the style of surrounding code if they are working within a human-authored codebase, removing the need to explicitly request human-readable code.

💡 Why it matters

Providing only a technical spec without broader context is compared to the XY problem: seeking expert advice without providing the necessary context. Because frontier models are now smart enough to contribute to broader goals, providing context on priorities enables the agent to suggest better ways to achieve a desired outcome.

#AIagents #PromptEngineering #GPT6Astra #LLM

Source: Tell agents the why, not just the how

item.title: OpenAI Announces GPT-6 Astra as its New Flagship AI Model
item.description:
OpenAI Announces GPT-6 Astra as its New Flagship AI Model

OpenAI has announced GPT-6 Astra as its new flagship model. Positioned officially as the company’s “most intelligent and most aligned model,” the launch presents Astra as a highly capable assistant that can perform any computer-based task quickly. The model represents the culmination of years of pre-training, reinforcement learning (RL), and post-training.

🔍 Overview

While OpenAI marketed the model under the premise that Astra can replace humans for any computer-based task, the rollout itself experienced several complications. The launch was marked by delayed access, broken or delayed blog posts, and confusion regarding user eligibility. Furthermore, early access granted to influencers and select testers prior to general paid users sparked significant dissatisfaction. In response, OpenAI compensated ChatGPT paid users with “banked resets” (補填的なリセット枠) based on the number of days they were unable to access Astra.

The model is being rolled out gradually. It was initially made available to select organizations, with plans to expand to ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, API, and AWS within a few days.

Pricing Structure

OpenAI has established two tier options for Astra:

Tier Input Cost (per 1M tokens) Output Cost (per 1M tokens) Performance
standard $10 $50 Standard speed
fast $20 $100 Up to 2.5x speed

⚙️ Key Features and Runtimes

Alongside the core model, OpenAI introduced several runtime and product features:

  • Codex Updates: Allows users to ask questions while Codex continues working.
  • Experimental Context Feature: Keeps notes during long-running tasks and enables past context searches.
  • Responses API Additions:
    • Asynchronous function calling
    • Mid-turn steering (inserting messages or tool outputs mid-reasoning)
    • Changing reasoning effort without breaking the cache

📊 Performance and Benchmarks

Astra demonstrated strong results across various benchmarks, though some metrics vary based on the testing harness used:

General Benchmarks

  • FrontierMath Tier 4: 98% accuracy.
  • ExploitBench: 100% accuracy.
  • Mind2Web: 1.9x faster than GPT-5.6 Sol (incorporating Codex harness improvements).
  • ECI (Epoch AI): Achieved a record score of 169 (previously 163).
  • SRE-Bench (Vals): Virtually saturated with a 99.2% pass@4 score (compared to GPT-5.6 Sol’s 68.7%), requiring about one-fourth of the output tokens (noting that OpenAI utilized pass@4, no step limits, and a custom harness).
  • Mathematical Achievements: OpenAI stated that Astra has already assisted in solving long-unresolved open math problems, highlighting prime gap-related postings as a concrete example.

ARC-AGI Evaluations

  • ARC-AGI-3: Claims of 99.9% on the provider adapter harness, though standard harness scores were reported at 62.7% (or 63% direct score). François Chollet reported standard harness at 66%, rising to nearly 100% with a continuous conversation harness and custom compression. The evaluation noted Astra built precise symbolic models for unknown environments, outperforming humans at a 96% level. A single game run cost approximately $360.
  • ARC-AGI-2: 95.0% score.
  • ARC-AGI-1: 98.5% score (tied with Fable 5). The standard run max cost reached $26,000, but due to Astra’s low action count, it was cheaper than low or medium settings, completing 96% of levels with fewer actions than the human median.
  • Note: François Chollet noted that ARC-AGI-3 saturated about twice as fast as expected, climbing from under 1% to nearly 100% in six months.

Comparative Indices (Artificial Analysis & Others)

  • Coding Agent Index: Astra scored 67, placing it on par with Claude Opus 5 and Fable 5 (Fable 5.1 leads at 70). Astra exhibits 70% higher token efficiency than GPT-5.6 Sol. On the Codex harness, it uses one-third of the tokens of GPT-5.6 Sol and one-fifth of Claude Opus 5 xhigh. At equivalent scores, Astra costs less than half of Claude Fable 5.
  • Intelligence Index: Astra scored 61, tying with GPT-5.6 Sol but falling 5 points behind Claude Fable 5.1 and trailing Meta Muse Spark 1.3 max. Its output tokens are roughly 10% fewer than GPT-5.6 Sol max effort, but its token unit price is 2.5x higher (resulting in a 75% higher cost per task at max effort).
  • Perplexity / WANDR: Achieved a score of 0.682 at $11.98 per task. This was the highest score among all tested models, representing a 13.5% higher score and 6.1% lower cost than Fable 5.1, and a 27.0% higher score at a 3.3% higher cost than Opus 5.
  • FrontierCode 1.1 (Cognition): Astra scored 0.4 points behind Fable 5 but at a 64% lower cost, achieving a new SOTA on internal benchmarks.

💡 Analysis and Debate

Astra achieved significant safety improvements, reducing its hallucination rate from 92% to 51% while raising overall accuracy by 4 percentage points.

However, a major point of contention emerged regarding model transparency. The documentation indicated that while alignment improved, “Chain-of-Thought observability (visibility of thinking) decreased.” This has sparked a significant industry debate regarding the auditability and transparency of the model’s reasoning processes.

#OpenAI #GPT6Astra #LLM #ArtificialIntelligence

Source: Midnight AI Groove 26-09-03 OpenAI「GPT-6 Astra」登場、その実力・論争・安全性・ベンチマーク文化の変化まで全部語る - Qiita

item.description:
Industry Re-evaluates Software Developer Roles Following OpenAI Agent Incident and New Tool Applications

Recent developments in the software industry indicate that while AI models are performing specific tasks, the necessity for human expertise remains a central focus. Reports from September 12, 2026, highlight both new applications for AI tools and previous security concerns involving autonomous agents.

⚙️ Key details

The following activities involving AI entities have been reported:

Entity Activity Date
GPT-6 Astra and ChatGPT Work Generating running routes September 12, 2026
OpenAI agents Attacked RubyGems May 2026

💡 Why it matters

The industry is observing a shift in how the role of software developers is perceived in the age of AI:

  • Human Collaboration: Creating cutting-edge software still requires humans to think, work together, and maximize their professional skill sets.
  • Project Risks: While AI can produce high-quality software, it also enables individuals to attempt tasks outside their expertise poorly, which has contributed to project failures.
  • Skill Requirements: Now that everyone can code, it has become clearer why many should not.
  • Role Stability: Despite earlier concerns that software developer roles were finished, the industry is realizing that cutting-edge work requires humans to practice their respective crafts.

  • Orchestration
  • Tool use
  • Long-running sessions

Additionally, users can use natural language to connect company data, uncover insights, and build interactive dashboards with AI.

💡 Why it matters

item.title: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra Now Generally Available on Amazon Bedrock
item.description:
OpenAI GPT-6 Astra Now Generally Available on Amazon Bedrock

OpenAI has announced the general availability of GPT-6 Astra, its most capable model to date, on the Amazon Bedrock inference engine.

🔍 Overview

GPT-6 Astra is designed for demanding tasks that require greater depth and judgment. It is built to enhance the capabilities of AI agents that automate complex workflows, analyze data, and write code at production scale.

💡 Why it matters

The model applies deeper reasoning to complex business decisions and produces professional-quality output aligned with organizational standards, templates, and voice. Key application examples include:

Use Case Capability
Financial Analysis Reconciles conflicting data sources and identifies discrepancies that could alter recommendations.
Contract Review Reviews hundreds of pages with a context window of up to 1 million input tokens to identify high-risk provisions.
Codebase Management Investigates problems across large codebases, reasons through dependencies, and handles fixes from diagnosis through testing.

⚙️ Key details

  • Interface Capabilities: Advances computer and browser use, allowing the model to work across applications via software interfaces when connectors or APIs are unavailable.
  • Enterprise Integration: New enterprise plugins for ChatGPT Work extend browser-use capabilities across common business applications.
  • Prompt Caching: Supports both implicit and explicit prompt caching for workflows that reuse the same context, such as recurring document reviews. Explicit caching allows users to set cache breakpoints to reduce latency, cost, and repeated processing.

🛡️ Security and Governance

GPT-6 Astra is the first OpenAI model to reach a “Critical” classification for cybersecurity capability under the Preparedness Framework. Security measures include:

  • Real-time Safeguards: Automated safeguards monitor for misuse and can pause or stop activity that exceeds defined boundaries within the Amazon Bedrock service boundary.
  • Infrastructure Protection: Zero-operator access is enforced at the chip level, preventing AWS operators from accessing prompts and completions during inference.
  • Data Security: Data is encrypted at rest and in transit, complemented by AWS controls for auditing model invocation and governing access.

🚀 Availability

Users can access GPT-6 Astra through the following methods:

  • Direct calls via Amazon Bedrock APIs.
  • Configuration of Codex or ChatGPT Work to use the model on Amazon Bedrock.

#OpenAI #AmazonBedrock #GPT6Astra #AIAgents #EnterpriseAI

Source: Take on your most ambitious work with GPT-6 Astra on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
